exam.subject: Biology
exam.title: Biology 1998

parts.title: Part I – Multiple Choice Questions
parts.instructions: Part I of the 1998 paper has 70 equal-mark questions. This file keeps only items whose stem, five options and answer were clear.

source.document: Google Drive Biology/1998_Biology.pdf (same scan also filed as Physics Matriculation/1998_Physics.pdf)
source.scan: HP Scan image PDF; Part I MCQs typed from OCR of page images

exam.answer_key_note: No official key in the PDF. Answers solved independently. Items with ambiguous OCR or two defensible options were skipped (6, 20, 31, 34, 48, 56, 60 and a few others).

questions.stem: Morphology is the branch of biology concerned with:
explanation_steps: Morphology is the study of the form and structure of organisms.
Taxonomy, behaviour, fossils and development are other branches. Answer: B.

questions.stem: A control experiment:

options.A: is a repeat of the original experiment to make sure the results are reproducible.
options.B: is carried out at a constant temperature.
options.C: is always carried out under the controlled conditions of a laboratory.
options.D: helps to interpret the results of the main experiment.
options.E: is simpler than a real experiment.

explanation_steps: A control is run so the result of the main experiment can be compared with a baseline.
It is not merely a repeat, a temperature hold, or a simpler version. Answer: D.

questions.stem: Adaptation is the process by which:

options.A: new varieties of plants are selected for use in agriculture.
options.B: organisms become better suited to their environment.
options.C: individuals of one species interact with individuals of another species.
options.D: a reflex reaction occurs in response to an unusual stimulus.
options.E: non-biological parents care for a child.

explanation_steps: Adaptation is the process that makes organisms better suited to their environment. Answer: B.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements is not true of cell theory?

options.A: The cell is the structural unit of life.
options.B: The cell is the unit of function of living things.
options.D: The molecules of life are the products of cellular activity.
options.E: Cells are surrounded by a cell wall.

explanation_steps: Cell theory does not claim that every cell has a wall. Animal cells have a membrane but no wall.
A–D are standard statements of cell theory. Answer: E.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements is true?

options.A: Plant cells are usually smaller than animal cells.
options.B: Animal cells tend to be more distinct in shape than plant cells.
options.C: Cytoplasm takes up most of the space in an animal cell.
options.D: Glycogen is stored in plant and animal cells.
options.E: Starch is stored in animal cells.

explanation_steps: Animal cells lack a large central vacuole, so cytoplasm occupies most of the cell.
Plant cells are usually larger and more regular; glycogen is animal storage; starch is plant storage. Answer: C.

questions.stem: According to the modern classification of organisms, humans are members of:
explanation_steps: Humans belong to phylum Chordata.
Vertebrata is a subphylum, Primates an order, Hominidae a family, and Homo a genus. Answer: A.

questions.stem: Algae:

options.B: occur in most permanent or semi-permanent bodies of water.
options.C: have specialised tissues for conducting water and food.

explanation_steps: Algae are mostly aquatic and occur in permanent or semi-permanent water.
They lack vascular tissue, can reproduce sexually, and are usually photosynthetic. Answer: B.

questions.stem: Yeasts:

options.A: refer to several kinds of fungi that form mycelium.
options.C: are major parasites of crop plants, particularly the cereals.
options.D: are used in the process of industrial fermentation.

explanation_steps: Yeasts are used in baking and industrial fermentation.
They are typically unicellular (no mycelium), lack chlorophyll, and are not the main cereal parasites. Answer: D.

questions.stem: Bryophytes differ from pteridophytes in that bryophytes:

options.E: lack specialised tissues for conducting water and food.

explanation_steps: Bryophytes are non-vascular: they lack specialised conducting tissues.
Both groups have chlorophyll, alternation of generations and sexual reproduction. Answer: E.

questions.stem: Monocots and dicots are the same in their:
explanation_steps: Both are angiosperms and produce seeds.
They differ in cotyledons, venation, bundle arrangement and root systems. Answer: C.

questions.stem: An example of nastic movement in plants is:

options.A: roots grow down, while shoots grow up.
options.B: the closing of a flower in the evening.
options.E: root growth towards water or nutrients.

explanation_steps: Nastic movements are non-directional responses, such as flowers closing in the evening.
A, D and E are tropisms; C is a mechanical bend. Answer: B.

questions.stem: Transpiration refers to:

options.A: the transportation of water from roots to leaves.
options.B: the evaporation of water from above-ground parts of a plant.
options.C: the exchange of gases that takes place at the surface of a leaf.
options.D: the absorption of water through non-root parts of the plant.
options.E: the transport of nutrients through the vascular system of a plant.

explanation_steps: Transpiration is the loss of water vapour from aerial parts of the plant. Answer: B.

questions.stem: Mitosis ensures that:

options.B: children are genetically different from their parents.
options.C: each new body cell has the same genetic make-up as its parent cell.
options.D: gametes are produced for the next generation.

explanation_steps: Mitosis produces daughter cells with the same chromosome set as the parent cell.
Halving and genetic difference belong to meiosis. Answer: C.

questions.stem: In the second division of meiosis:
explanation_steps: Meiosis II separates sister chromatids, like mitosis.
Homologues pair and separate in meiosis I, which halves the chromosome number. Answer: A.

questions.stem: In parthenogenesis:

options.A: two parents are required to produce each offspring.
options.C: the offspring are genetically different from the parents.
options.D: an unfertilised egg develops into an embryo.
options.E: a single-celled organism divides into two equal daughter cells.

explanation_steps: Parthenogenesis is development of an embryo from an unfertilised egg. Answer: D.

questions.stem: The specialised organs of animals that give rise to gametes are called the:
explanation_steps: Gonads are the organs that produce gametes. Sperm and ova are the gametes themselves. Answer: C.

questions.stem: The HIV virus is known to be spread by:
explanation_steps: HIV is transmitted by blood and body fluids, including contaminated instruments.
It is not spread by clothes, ordinary touch, or coughing. Answer: C.

questions.stem: Of the human reproductive hormones, the corpus luteum is the main source of:
explanation_steps: After ovulation the corpus luteum secretes progesterone (and some estrogen).
FSH and LH come from the pituitary. Answer: A.

questions.stem: From outer to inner, the order of flower structures is:
explanation_steps: A typical flower, outside in, is sepal, petal, stamen, carpel. Answer: D.

questions.stem: The germination of seeds takes place in the absence of:
explanation_steps: Most seeds germinate without light. Water, oxygen and a suitable temperature are required.
Inhibitors must be inactivated, so germination does not occur in their presence. Answer: D.

questions.stem: In one of Mendel's crosses, all self-pollinated F1 plants were green. In the F2 generation, Mendel counted 428 green plants and 152 yellow plants. These results can be explained by:
explanation_steps: 428:152 is about 3:1, a single-trait ratio.
That ratio needs dominance (green over yellow) and segregation of alleles.
Independent assortment needs two traits. Answer: E.

questions.stem: In the fruit fly, gray body is dominant over black body. Two gray flies were mated to produce 158 gray and 49 black offspring. Both gray parents must have been:
explanation_steps: 158:49 is about 3:1, so both parents carried a hidden black allele.
Both were heterozygous. Answer: C.

questions.stem: The power of selection in modifying populations over time can be demonstrated by:

options.B: field observations and experiments in natural environments.
options.D: the response of bacteria to antibiotics.

explanation_steps: Artificial selection, field studies, lab selection and antibiotic resistance all show selection changing populations. Answer: E.

questions.stem: An example of a structure which is not vestigial is:

options.A: the eyes of a fish that lives in a cave where there is no sunlight.
options.E: the muscles that move human ears.

explanation_steps: Mitochondria are functioning organelles, not vestigial structures.
Cave-fish eyes, the appendix, the coccyx and ear-moving muscles are classic vestigial examples in this syllabus. Answer: D.

questions.stem: In ecological studies, a community refers to:

options.A: a group of individuals within a species living in a particular place at the same time.
options.B: the complex of interactions between living and non-living parts of the environment.
options.C: a group of families within a species living in a particular place at the same time.
options.D: an extended family which depends upon one another for food and shelter.
options.E: populations of organisms that live together in a specific area and depend upon one another.

explanation_steps: A community is the populations of different species living together in one area.
A is a population; B is closer to an ecosystem. Answer: E.

questions.stem: An example of a food chain in nature from producer → primary consumer → secondary consumer → tertiary consumer is:
explanation_steps: Weeds are producers; tadpoles eat plant material; water beetles eat tadpoles; pike eat the beetles.
Sunlight is not an organism, and a saprophyte is not a tertiary consumer. Answer: A.

questions.stem: In relation to ecological pyramids:

options.A: the number of consumers is always less than the number of producers.
options.B: the number of consumers is always greater than the number of producers.
options.C: producer biomass is always greater than consumer biomass.
options.D: energy availability is greatest at the highest trophic level.
options.E: there is less energy available to the next highest trophic level.

explanation_steps: Energy is lost at each transfer, so the next trophic level has less energy available.
Numbers and biomass pyramids can be inverted. Answer: E.

questions.stem: Soil erosion may be controlled or reduced by:

options.B: increasing the amount of water runoff.

explanation_steps: Vegetation cover holds soil and reduces runoff. Clearing land increases erosion. Answer: D.

questions.stem: As part of our diet, water is useful in the following way:

options.A: water is a source of energy.
options.B: water dissolves many compounds and thereby makes them available for chemical reactions.
options.C: water helps in hydrolysis of carbohydrates into their building units, monosaccharides.
options.D: water helps us to regulate our body temperature.

explanation_steps: Water is not a fuel, so it is not an energy source.
It is a solvent, takes part in hydrolysis, and is used in temperature regulation. Answer: E.

questions.stem: What would happen if a person's bile duct became blocked?

options.D: The duodenum contents would be neutralised more quickly.

explanation_steps: Bile emulsifies fats. A blocked bile duct reduces fat digestion.
It does not mainly block carbohydrate or protein digestion, and bile is alkaline so neutralisation would be slower. Answer: B.

questions.stem: Nucleases are enzymes which can break down _____ into their smaller units:
explanation_steps: Nucleases hydrolyse nucleic acids, DNA or RNA. Answer: B.

questions.stem: The main function of the finger-like projections known as villi on the wall of the small intestine is:

options.B: to promote food absorption by increasing the surface area of the small intestine.
options.C: to promote food absorption by decreasing the surface area of the small intestine.

explanation_steps: Villi increase the absorptive surface of the small intestine. Answer: B.

questions.stem: The formation of a blood clot is due to the change of:
explanation_steps: Clotting converts soluble fibrinogen into insoluble fibrin threads. Answer: B.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements is true?

options.A: All antigens are foreign substances capable of causing damage to the human body.
options.B: Antigens are foreign substances which make the body produce antibodies.
options.C: Antibodies against measles can protect a person against malaria.
options.D: Antibodies are manufactured by blood platelets.

explanation_steps: An antigen is a substance that stimulates antibody production.
Not every antigen damages the body, antibodies are specific, and they are made by lymphocytes, not platelets. Answer: B.

questions.stem: It is more desirable to breathe through the nose than through the mouth because:

options.A: we can take in more air through the nose than through the mouth.
options.B: dust and bacteria get filtered out as the air passes through the nasal cavity.
options.C: the air gets warmed and moistened as it passes through the nasal cavity.

explanation_steps: The nose filters dust and bacteria and warms and moistens the air.
It does not take in more air than the mouth. Answer: E.

questions.stem: Which of the following activities in the skin help our body to warm up when the temperature of the air around us is low?

options.A: The arterioles in the dermis contract and flow of blood is reduced under the skin.
options.B: The hairs on the surface of the body are erected.
options.C: Loss of heat is avoided by excessive sweating.

explanation_steps: Vasoconstriction and hair erection reduce heat loss.
Sweating increases heat loss, so it does not warm the body. Answer: E.

questions.stem: Which of the following organs are major excretory organs of the human body?
explanation_steps: Lungs, liver, kidneys and skin all excrete wastes.
The pancreas and thyroid are not major excretory organs. Answer: E.

questions.stem: Urine leaves the kidney through the ______ and enters the bladder.
explanation_steps: Urine passes from the kidney to the bladder in the ureter. The urethra leaves the bladder. Answer: C.

questions.stem: The urine of a person who eats one of the following will contain more urea:
explanation_steps: Urea comes from deamination of amino acids. A high-protein food such as meat raises urea output. Answer: D.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements is true?

options.A: In a bright light the iris of your eye closes down.
options.B: In a bright light the pupil narrows down.
options.C: In dim light the iris of your eye opens.
options.D: In dim light the pupil widens.

explanation_steps: Bright light constricts the pupil (iris closes down); dim light dilates the pupil. All four statements match that reflex. Answer: E.

questions.stem: Neurons that conduct signals from the brain and spinal cord to muscles are known as:
explanation_steps: Motor neurons carry impulses from the CNS to effectors such as muscles. Answer: C.

questions.stem: The hormone responsible for the normal development of secondary sex characteristics in males is:
explanation_steps: Testosterone produces male secondary sexual characteristics. Answer: A.

questions.stem: When your nose gets irritated you start sneezing. This is an example of:
explanation_steps: Sneezing is an automatic response to irritation: a simple reflex. Answer: B.

questions.stem: The parasite, Plasmodium, that causes malaria belongs to the phylum:
explanation_steps: In the classification used on this paper, Plasmodium is a protozoan.
Sporozoa is a class within the protozoa, not the phylum named in the stem. Answer: D.

questions.stem: One of the following organisms represents the simplest form of multicellular organism:
explanation_steps: Sponges are the simplest multicellular animals. Plasmodium is unicellular. Answer: B.

questions.stem: One of the features of the worms that distinguish them from phyla which are more primitive in evolutionary development is:
explanation_steps: Worms are bilaterally symmetrical. More primitive animals such as cnidarians are radial. Answer: C.

questions.stem: Proper disposal of human waste and use of latrines may not have an effect in preventing one of the following diseases:
explanation_steps: Leishmaniasis is spread by sandflies, not by faeces.
Amoebiasis, taeniasis and schistosomiasis are linked to poor sanitation. Answer: A.

questions.stem: The Arthropoda phylum includes all of the following animals except the:
explanation_steps: A snail is a mollusc. Mosquitoes, scorpions, grasshoppers and spiders are arthropods. Answer: E.

questions.stem: The primitive chordates differ from the vertebrates in that:
explanation_steps: Primitive chordates have a notochord and pharyngeal slits but no vertebral column.
Only A is a difference. Answer: A.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements is true?

options.A: Amphibians can breathe through the skin and lung.
options.B: Reptiles can only breathe through the lung.
options.C: Reptiles do not require water for reproduction.
options.D: Amphibians spend part of their life cycle in water because water is necessary for reproduction.

explanation_steps: Amphibians use skin and lungs and need water for eggs and early life.
Reptiles breathe with lungs and lay shelled eggs on land. Answer: E.

questions.stem: The ability that one of the fingers (thumb) can touch each of the other fingers is a characteristic of:
explanation_steps: An opposable thumb is a primate feature, not a feature of all placental mammals or of whales. Answer: B.

questions.stem: In which of the following environments are bacteria absent?

options.C: On the surface of our body.

explanation_steps: Bacteria occur in air, food, on skin, and thermophiles live in hot springs. Answer: E.

questions.stem: One of the characteristics that distinguishes a bacterial cell from an amoeba is lack of a:
explanation_steps: Bacteria are prokaryotes: they have no nuclear membrane.
They do have a cell membrane, cytoplasm and a chromosome. Answer: D.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a wrong statement?

options.A: In animals excess carbohydrates are stored in the liver and muscles as glycogen.
options.B: In animals excess carbohydrates are stored as fat in adipose tissue.
options.C: Glycogen and starch provide the body with vitamins.
options.D: Monosaccharides are for carbohydrates as amino acids are for proteins.
options.E: In plants carbohydrates are stored as starch.

explanation_steps: Glycogen and starch are energy stores, not vitamin sources.
A, B, D and E are correct. Answer: C.

questions.stem: An abnormally high count of white blood cells in a person's blood may indicate that the person:

options.A: has got some sort of infection.
options.B: has eaten a high carbohydrate diet.

explanation_steps: A high white-cell count can mean infection or leukemia.
It is not caused by a high-carbohydrate meal, and anaemia is a low red-cell condition. Answer: E.

questions.stem: The largest structure in the human brain is the:
explanation_steps: The cerebrum is the largest part of the human brain. Answer: A.

questions.stem: How many different pieces of bones are there in the human body?
explanation_steps: The adult human skeleton has 206 bones. Answer: A.

questions.stem: In the life cycle of Schistosoma, the stage that enters the human body is known as:
explanation_steps: Cercariae leave the snail and penetrate human skin.
The miracidium infects the snail; the egg leaves in faeces or urine. Answer: A.

questions.stem: Catabolism and anabolism are:

options.B: two phases of digestion taking place at different times.
options.C: two opposite phases of metabolism taking place at the same time.
options.D: two phases of digestion concerned with the movement and absorption of food.
options.E: harmful to an organism when working as opposites.

explanation_steps: Anabolism builds molecules and catabolism breaks them down. Both run together as metabolism. Answer: C.

questions.stem: The cells of human bodies contain:
explanation_steps: Human somatic cells have 46 chromosomes, which is 23 pairs.
Of those, 22 pairs are autosomes. Answer: B.

questions.stem: RNA differs from DNA in all except one of the following.

options.B: commonly occurs as a single stranded molecule
options.D: directly involved in the translation of genetic messages

explanation_steps: Both nucleic acids use the same phosphate group.
They differ in sugar, strand number, bases, and the direct role of RNA in translation. Answer: E.

questions.stem: Physical factors affecting an ecosystem include:
explanation_steps: Temperature, light, altitude and climate are abiotic factors.
Competition, predators and microbes are biotic. Answer: E.

questions.stem: Grasslands are:

options.C: found in areas where rainfall is too low to support a community of trees.

explanation_steps: Grasslands occur where rainfall supports grass but is too low for a closed tree community.
They do support large herbivores. Answer: C.
